claims.statement: The ci.yml workflow runs reusable test, lint, and documentation-link workflows plus merge-conflict, cross-reference, external documentation URL, and generated-file checks on pull requests and pushes to main.

The CI workflow uses GitHub's concurrency feature with group strategy to cancel earlier runs in favor of newer ones when multiple pushes occur to the same PR or branch, reducing queue time and resource usage.

The check-generated-files job in ci.yml verifies regenerated files match checked-in versions, with bypass capability via bypass-auto-check label and automatic skip for github-actions[bot] package download updates.

The Test Code Samples workflow is triggered by code-sample or workflow-file pull-request changes, manual dispatch, and a monthly schedule; its credential-dependent job skips fork PRs, internal PRs select changed supported sample files from the merge base, and manual or scheduled runs test all samples.

Monthly and manual full code-sample runs enable LangSmith tracing; snippet regeneration runs when the test was not cancelled, fewer than 20 samples failed, and at least one trace was updated, after which a trace-refresh PR may be maintained.

Code-sample trace publication is limited to single-snippet source files: multi-snippet files are recorded as skipped, while a selected agent-like LangSmith root run is publicly shared and stored in the trace-link manifest.

The scheduled package-download workflow keeps generation read-only until a second job consumes its short-lived artifact; when generated package and integration surfaces differ, that job creates a timestamped PR and enables squash auto-merge.

Package-download maintenance creates Linear hosted-documentation candidate tickets only when both the Linear API-key secret and team-key variable are configured; without either value it runs candidate detection in dry-run mode.
The daily LangSmith OpenAPI refresh reuses its standing branch and appends to an existing open refresh PR, creating a new PR only when no such PR exists and the processed specification changed.

The code-sample runner retries a LangSmith 429 response up to a configurable default of five attempts and treats persistent rate limiting as a skipped sample; ordinary sample failures fail the runner, while trace-collection failures are reported as warnings without failing it.

The reusable test and lint workflows make shallow checkouts, synchronize the `test` dependency group, and run `make test` or `make lint` using caller-supplied Python and working-directory inputs; the reusable link workflow instead has read-only contents permission, a 20-minute limit, Python and Node setup, and runs Mintlify link and OpenAPI checks.

The OpenAPI refresh processor fetches only from the allowlisted LangSmith API host and deterministically hides configured internal operations, normalizes visible titles, and groups and orders tags before writing the generated specification.

The PR welcome workflow is a pull_request_target workflow that reads OWNERS from the PR base ref and changed-file metadata through GitHub APIs, applies last-match ownership rules, and can request only opted-in owners other than the PR author without checking out PR code.

The external-integration pull_request_target workflow does not check out or execute PR code: it uses API file metadata and an organization-membership App token to label qualifying external integration PRs, reads added MDX only as bytes to detect featured frontmatter, and otherwise posts an idempotent listing-form redirect before closing the PR.

Integration submission automation begins only from manual dispatch or the integration-run label, verifies the triggering actor has write-level repository permission before checkout, and prevents duplicate processing with the integration-automation label.

After maintainer authorization, integration submission automation parses issue-form data as untrusted metadata and directs the agent to leave local edits only; parse, blocker, agent, and no-diff outcomes are reported on the issue, while a real diff alone lets the workflow create and link a review PR.

The package-download generator refreshes package counts only when their download timestamp is older than 24 hours, then regenerates the provider overview and integration download tables before artifact handoff.

After successful snippet regeneration on a full run, the code-sample workflow compares trace artifacts against the standing chore/refresh-code-sample-traces branch and appends a commit to its open PR or creates that review PR only when the manifest or generated snippets differ.

The PR template asks contributors to describe the change and related work and, where applicable, confirm local documentation validation, tested examples, root-relative internal links, and navigation updates; it identifies preview deployment as an optional internal-team action.

The HTML export workflow is a read-only weekly or manual job that checks out without persisted credentials, prepares Python, Node 22, Mintlify, and htmltest, and runs `make export-htmltest`; that Make target builds, exports, unpacks, and checks only external URLs.

The HTML-export and code-sample Linear workflows react only to scheduled upstream failures or cancellations, create a Linear issue using configured secrets and the upstream run URL, and deliberately do not ticket manual or PR runs.

Scheduled and manual full code-sample runs have a 150-minute limit while pull-request runs have a 60-minute limit, and the workflow supplies PostgreSQL plus Python, Node, Java/JBang, and Go tooling before invoking the sample target.

Hosted-documentation candidate creation checks current external integration download counts against a default 50,000-per-month threshold and skips creating a duplicate when a matching Linear issue is still open.

For an internal pull request, the code-sample workflow finds the merge base with the PR base branch and passes only changed supported source files under src/code-samples to the runner; a workflow-only trigger with no such paths reports no sample failures.

The code-sample workflow retains a failed full test step long enough to regenerate snippets when fewer than 20 samples failed and traces were updated, but its final step fails the job whenever that test step failed.

The Mintlify preview workflow builds only same-repository pull requests or manual dispatches, turns the build output into a uniquely named preview branch, triggers the Mintlify preview API, and removes matching preview branches when a PR closes.

The preview comment job replaces earlier bot preview comments and, when Mintlify returns a preview URL, lists at most five routable changed Markdown pages ranked by diff size while excluding code samples and snippets.
The publish workflow builds documentation on main pushes or manual dispatch and publishes a public directory containing build output to the prod branch.
The daily or manual OpenWiki update uses a full-history checkout, runs openwiki code --update, and creates or updates an openwiki/update PR limited to openwiki, AGENTS.md, and its workflow file.
